topic.title: Integrating Web Author with a DITA-aware CMS

body.p:
supports the use of some API extensions and a method from Oxygen XML Editor that can be used to customize nodes in the DITA Map view. The following extensions or methods are available:
ro.sync.exml.workspace.api.standalone.ditamap.TopicRefTargetInfoProvider - This API extension provides titles for topic references. A CMS that already caches topic titles in its database can implement it as an optimization. By default, Web Author fetches each topic from the CMS, parses it, and extracts its title.
ro.sync.exml.workspace.api.editor.page.ditamap.DITAMapNodeRendererCustomizer - This API extension customizes how information appears in the DITA Map view (for example, titles for topic references). This method is called after Web Author computes the title for topic references.
ro.sync.ecss.extensions.api.webapp.access.WebappPluginWorkspace.setDITAKeyDefinitionManagerProvider - This method sets an object that provides a DITA key manager for each open document. It overrides the default Web Author behavior, which fetches the main DITA map and all nested submaps from the CMS, parses them, and determines the keys.

section.title: Setting the DITA Context Used to Load the Editor
section.p: You have two options for opening a topic in a specific DITA context:

ul.li: Use the ditamap and dita.val.url URL parameters added to the OXY-URL.
Use the workspace.getEditingContextManager() JavaScript API. A sample plugin that uses this API to set the DITA Map for some popular repository layouts is available on GitHub: .
